episodes.169895: An upper level low pressure system moved along the Canadian border throughout the day.  This feature dragged a cold front through Montana that set off multiple thunderstorms.  Some of the storms became severe and one generated a tornado that impacted the town of Glentana.
episodes.170488: Strong thunderstorms that developed along the sea breeze collision moved east and offshore of Volusia County. One storm became severe where it produced wind damage in Edgewater.
episodes.170489: A line of strong thunderstorms that developed along the sea breeze collision moved east and over Brevard County. Several of these storms produced strong wind gusts along the Intracoastal Waterway.
episodes.170490: Lightning struck and injured two people at two different locations in New Smyrna Beach. A 27-year-old man was seriously injured and transported to a local hospital, where he later died from his injuries. A 66-year-old man suffered minor injuries after lightning struck nearby.
episodes.170671: A cold front moved across a moderately unstable air mass across Ontario province into northwest NY during the afternoon and early evening of July 19th. Scattered thunderstorms moved from Ontario into St. Lawrence county NY with several reports of damaging winds in the form of downed trees and powerlines.
episodes.170865: Several bands of thunderstorms containing gusty winds developed along a cold front.
episodes.170973: Thunderstorms developed during the early evening hours on Monday (7/18) across north-central Wisconsin near a frontal boundary.  The strongest storms produced hail up to penny size across Vilas County.
episodes.171122: A cluster of thunderstorms impacted Clay County during the early morning hours of July 19th. A home in Pheba sustained wind damage to a pool deck and fence.
episodes.171320: Strong summer low pressure drew a cold front across the region during the afternoon of the 19th. A strong upper level disturbance also crossed the region along with the cold front. Thunderstorms developed during the afternoon. Several of the thunderstorms reached severe levels...producing damaging winds. The most extensive wind damage occurred across northeast Aroostook county along the Route 1 corridor from Mars Hill...to Bridgewater...to Monticello. Several reports of tree damage occurred in this area.
episodes.171495: A few wind gusts over 60 mph occurred with a thunderstorm that tracked across parts of northeastern Campbell County.
episodes.171712: Southwest steering flow and plenty of moisture at the surface and aloft led to scattered to numerous showers and storms that tracked Gulf Coast during the morning under SW steering flow toward the Atlantic Coastal Waters into the evening, with storm enhancement when lake, river, sea breezes and outflows merged during the afternoon and evening hours.
episodes.171714: Southwest steering flow and plenty of moisture at the surface and aloft led to scattered to numerous showers and storms that tracked Gulf Coast during the morning under SW steering flow toward the Atlantic Coastal Waters into the evening, with storm enhancement when lake, river, sea breezes and outflows merged during the afternoon and evening hours.
episodes.171715: Southwest steering flow and plenty of moisture at the surface and aloft led to scattered to numerous showers and storms that tracked Gulf Coast during the morning under SW steering flow toward the Atlantic Coastal Waters into the evening, with storm enhancement when lake, river, sea breezes and outflows merged during the afternoon and evening hours.
episodes.171804: Thunderstorms developed along the sea breeze on the coast of southeast South Carolina in the early afternoon hours. The thunderstorms then gradually shifted further inland along outflow boundaries. These thunderstorms produced damaging wind gusts.
episodes.171805: Thunderstorms developed along the sea breeze on the coast of southeast Georgia in the early afternoon hours. The thunderstorms then gradually shifted further inland along outflow boundaries. These thunderstorms produced damaging wind gusts.
episodes.171806: Thunderstorms developed along the sea breeze on the coast of southeast South Carolina and southeast Georgia in the early afternoon hours, producing strong wind gusts. The thunderstorms eventually shifted offshore and produced more strong wind gusts over the Atlantic coastal waters in the late afternoon.
episodes.172005: A cold front moving across a very warm, moist and unstable airmass produced strong to severe thunderstorms over west half portions of Upper Michigan during the late evening of the 18th and early morning of the 19th.
episodes.172022: A cold front moving across the Upper Great Lakes generated strong to severe thunderstorms over mainly west half portions of Lake Superior from the late evening of the 18th into the morning of the 19th.
episodes.172045: A shortwave trough moved eastward through the region. Showers and thunderstorms were numerous across the area. A few storms were severe, causing heavy rainfall, large hail and damaging wind.
episodes.172181: Isolated strong to severe thunderstorms tracked across far northeast ND and far northwest MN through the early to mid afternoon hours. Storms produced areas of heavy rain, downburst winds, and at least one brief tornado.
episodes.172206: Severe thunderstorms moved from northeast Montana into northwest North Dakota ahead of an upper level low, spreading into north central North Dakota as a low-level jet increased in intensity. During the initial storms, damaging winds were the main threat. The strongest winds were estimated at 95 mph over the Wildrose area in Williams County where outbuildings were damaged, sheet metal detached from buildings damaged vehicles, and trees were uprooted and snapped. Later, storms had a mix of hail and damaging wind gusts. The largest hail reported was three inches in diameter, causing damage in the Williston area of Williams County.
episodes.172284: Scattered thunderstorms due to an upper level trough moved over the James River and produced gusty winds on July 19.
episodes.172326: An upper level storm system passing to our north, combined with afternoon instability and marginal shear allowed for a few severe storms to form and produce localized damaging winds.
episodes.172627: Another active setup in mid-late July resulted in numerous microburst related wind gusts in portions of Utah's West Desert Region, as well as a report of severe hail. Additionally, flash flooding was noted in southern Utah. This also coincided with a period of anomalous heat across much of the region.
episodes.172728: A warm front advanced across New Hampshire during the evening of July 18th, putting southern New Hampshire in a warm and unstable airmass. The unstable airmass was associated with strong dynamics aloft which brought a high shear environment.|These ingredients combined to support rotating thunderstorms across southwest New Hampshire which led to a brief touchdown of a tornado in Chesterfield, near Spofford Lake, NH.
episodes.172817: Severe thunderstorms formed during the late evening in eastern North Dakota, then expanded in coverage through the overnight hours. Portions of far northwestern Minnesota were impacted by this same system after midnight.
episodes.172818: Severe thunderstorms formed during the late evening in eastern North Dakota, then expanded in coverage through the overnight hours. Portions of far northwestern Minnesota were impacted by this same system after midnight.
episodes.172899: Thunderstorms produced high winds and damage in southwest Alabama.
episodes.172943: Scattered thunderstorms and storm clusters developed over western North Carolina during the afternoon and evening. A couple of the storms produced brief damaging wind gusts. Slow-moving storm cells also produced locally excessive rainfall in Union County.
episodes.172944: Scattered thunderstorms and storm clusters developed over upstate South Carolina during the afternoon and evening. A couple of the storms produced brief damaging wind gusts.
episodes.173069: Multiple waves of typical daytime summertime showers and thunderstorms developed within a modestly unstable and abnormally moist tropical airmass during the afternoon and evenings of July 19th through July 21st.  These storms produced numerous reports of trees and powerlines down, quarter size hail, and flash flooding across portions of north and central Georgia.

A very brief but damaging tornado touched down in Chesterfield, NH |Monday night as a thunderstorm moved through the area. EF-0 damage |was initially observed on Mill Pond Rd. before the tornado became |stronger and caused significant tree damage supporting EF-1 |classification just north of Mill Pond. The tornado began to lift |shortly after the EF-1 damage with sporadic EF-0 damage before |quickly ending. The tornado damaged approximately 200 trees with a |few outbuildings being destroyed on the property. Tree damage included |uprooted hardwoods and softwoods, along with snapped trees.  Fortunately |no permanent residential structural damage was reported besides debris |clean up.
